HQ: 2026 State of AI in Medicine Report
Type: 94% of physicians using or interested in AI. AI use rose from 47% to 63%. Literature search top use case (35%). 71% concerned about accuracy and reliability. 3151 physicians surveyed.
Published framework arguing clinical AI evaluation must go beyond benchmarks. Proposes clinical intent knowledge integrity and risk evaluation. Benchmarks often too generic for point-of-care fitness.

OpenEvidence launches EvidenceGrade - real-time GRADE-based grading and visualization of the strength of cited evidence beneath every AI answer. Builds on the GRADE framework used by Cochrane and WHO. Companion to existing Cochrane and AAO-HNSF partnerships. Differentiator vs ChatGPT for Clinicians and UpToDate Expert AI which do not surface per-citation evidence quality.

Weilnhammer et al. publish SIM-VAIL framework in Nature Medicine. 810 conversations across 9 frontier consumer chatbots (Claude ChatGPT Gemini Grok Llama families) and 30 simulated psychiatric profiles scored across 13 clinically-grounded risk dimensions. Concerning behavior widespread but reduced in newer models. First clinically-validated cross-vendor consumer chatbot audit. Does not directly benchmark OpenEvidence but creates external reference for evaluating OE-adjacent consumer tools (ChatGPT Health Copilot Health). Microsoft AI co-author. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42567928/

OpenEvidence publicly launches Visits (real-time evidence-grounded intelligence for the live patient visit) and wide-releases AI-integrated Doctor Dialer with HIPAA-grade messaging faxing and voicemail (Wayback snapshot 3 Aug 2026). Combined product wedge competes with ChatGPT for Clinicians UpToDate Expert AI Doximity Ask and EHR-native ambient AI; telemedicine wedge competes with Doximity Dialer Amwell and K Health PatientGPT. US-only (OE blocked in EU/UK under AI Act). https://web.archive.org/web/2026/https://www.openevidence.com/announcements/visits-real-time-medical-intelligence

HQ: PACT framework for clinical AI continuity
Type: Khairat and Safran (UNC Harvard) publish PACT framework (PMID 42552388) reframing clinical AI as a health-system function spanning pre-visit visit and post-visit care with ownership communication channels confirmation rules escalation pathways and outcome measures. Post-visit coordination identified as highest-impact near-term setting. Proposes tiered human support. Academic consensus signal that OE-class CDS will need to extend into longitudinal care continuity not just in-visit question answering. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42552388/
